claims.text: The target material is equimolar TaVCrW, with 25 at.% each of Ta, V, Cr, and W.
TaVCrW is considered in BCC solid and liquid states over 2000-2400 K.
The MTP will be trained on DFT energies, forces, and virials, including liquid configurations over a broad temperature range.
Replacing EAM and TI with MTP and FEP will reduce computational cost by more than 80% while retaining sub-meV/atom accuracy.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio configurational and vibrational phase-space distributions in both solid and liquid TaVCrW will allow FEP to converge with low variance.
The MTP must reproduce solid-state SRO and the liquid structure factor as part of the relevant phase-space distribution.
A supercell of at least 512 atoms is required to resolve SRO and avoid finite-size artifacts.
The validation temperature range must span 2000-2400 K to capture the solid-liquid transition.
The proposed simulations use a 1 fs time step and 20-30 intermediate lambda states for FEP.
Spin-polarized PBE training data will account for high-temperature magnetic fluctuations involving V and Cr.
An electronic temperature of 0.1 eV is sufficient to handle electronic smearing in the liquid.
The MTP captures complex many-body interactions and electronic or magnetic effects that EAM misses.
FEP produces the speedup by requiring fewer intermediate states and less sampling than TI when the MTP is sufficiently accurate.
Solid-state SRO stabilizes TaVCrW by approximately 2-3 meV/atom.
Electronic DOS effects near the Fermi level can shift the melting point by tens of kelvin, and spin-polarized DFT training will capture this effect.
The method will predict the TaVCrW melting point with less than 1 meV/atom free-energy error and within approximately 5 K of a DFT-TI baseline.
The full melting-point calculation will require less than 200 CPU-hours instead of approximately 1000 CPU-hours.
The method will recover 2-3 meV/atom of SRO stabilization and reproduce the DFT liquid structure factor within 5%.
Prior same-system work reports MTP-aided thermodynamic integration with a fourfold speedup and less than 1 meV/atom error.
The benchmark falsifies the hypothesis if the MTP+FEP versus DFT-TI free-energy discrepancy exceeds 0.5 meV/atom, the melting-point discrepancy exceeds 10 K, or the cost reduction is below 70%.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as TOR-TILD using EAM plus TI, but the cited fourfold speedup and sub-meV result is explicitly for MTP-aided TI. This conflates the original EAM reference workflow with the previously accelerated MTP+TI workflow.
The claimed cost target is greater than 80%, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis below 70%, leaving a 70-80% reduction as non-falsifying despite failure of the stated target.

The predicted melting-point accuracy is ±5 K, whereas deviations of 5-10 K do not falsify the hypothesis. Conversely, the 0.5 meV/atom falsification threshold is stricter than the stated sub-1 meV/atom accuracy target.
